correctness.rationale: The transfinite construction uses actual ordinal prefixes, not a finite-word extrapolation. With finitely many initial valuation colours, each noncofinal colour has a strict bound in the current ordinal prefix; their finite union defines a smaller prefix beta_(j+1). The strictly decreasing beta-sequence terminates after finitely many indices because ordinals admit no infinite descending omega-sequence. On each layer all present colours are cofinal. Each prefix is definable as diamond of the union of noncofinal colour classes in its predecessor; every candidate cell is therefore definable. Conversely, a nonempty union of whole cells has a highest occupied ordinal layer with a cofinal colour, so diamond sends it to the entire lower initial prefix; closure yields precisely the asserted 2^(sum|C_j|) algebra. Boundary includes zero beta, singleton successor tops, alpha=omega and omega+1, arbitrary nonzero set ordinals, q>=1. Fresh independent exhaustive Boolean/modal closure through 6,554 finite valuation words verified every predicted count.
residual_risks: The proof of strict descent uses finite colour set and well-founded ordinals; the finite checker alone would not prove the infinite case.
Requires reflexive forward order <= and finitely many Boolean generators; no claim for strict order or arbitrary posets.

value.rationale: The least modal-stable atom partition of an arbitrary finite colouring of a set ordinal is a natural invariant refining local finiteness into a constructive quotient and exact size. Successor stages above infinite limits create distinct cofinal layers, not captured by simply counting tail colours on omega. The theorem is reusable for explicit generated subalgebras and finite-model construction, rather than a renamed textbook result.
